result.reasoning:
REFUTED. The reporter's arithmetic reproduces, but every inferential step it rests on breaks, and the headline number/conclusion do not change.

REPRODUCED (so the raw numbers are not in dispute): seg_lowliq_m over 15 factors med +1.18 / mean +1.13 / up 87% / both 93%; base>=1 subset (F101,F102,F103,F105,F111) med +0.41 / mean +0.09 with per-factor +1.30/+0.41/+0.76/+0.15/-2.18; corr(base,d) = -0.84; variant abs sharpe med +1.84 sd 0.64 vs base med +0.70 sd 1.11; k_known = +2.2242.

R-A. The "-2.18 on the best base" is a direction-mismatch artifact, not a case where the action hurts a good base. /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/sweep.py:111-116 builds seg_lowliq_p = cs_first_low40(X, LIQ) and seg_lowliq_m = cs_first_low40(neg(X), LIQ), and sweep.py:146-150 LOCKS sign = +1 for every cs_first_*/cs_last_* variant. So "_m" equals "the factor's own direction" only for the 14 factors whose base sign is -1. F111 is the one factor with base sign +1, so seg_lowliq_m applies the REVERSED direction to it. Its direction-matched twin is seg_lowliq_p = +2.19 against base +2.15, i.e. d = +0.04, not -2.18. Direction-matched statistics: all 15 -> med +1.18, mean +1.28, 15/15 positive, 0% down, 100% both-segments-up; base>=1 -> med +0.41, mean +0.53, 0% down, 100% both, and 5/5 absolute levels rise (1.37->2.67, 2.05->2.45, 1.49->2.25, 1.96->2.11, 2.15->2.19). The claimed "mean +0.09" and "F111 drops 2.18" are both artifacts; the published +1.18 is unchanged by the same correction.

R-B. The evidence line "only F101's +2.67 is above +2.22, 14 of 15 below" is false on the reporter's own table: F101 +2.67, F102 +2.45 and F103 +2.25 all exceed k_known = +2.2242. 3 above, 12 at/below (identical for the direction-matched set).

R-C. The "regression effect" mechanism is statistically void. d = variant - base forces a strongly negative corr(base,d) whenever sd(variant) < sd(base). Monte-Carlo null with the variant level drawn INDEPENDENTLY of the base at the observed mean/sd: corr(base,d) = -0.94 mean, 95% range [-0.98,-0.88]; observed is -0.94 direction-matched / -0.84 published — inside the independence null, so it carries no information about regression. corr(base,variant) is only +0.20 on the published id. A genuine regression-to-the-mean null (shrink the base toward its own mean, no level shift) gives d median -0.04 and P(all 15 positive) ~ 0.0000, against an observed 15/15 positive and a level shift of the whole population from +0.70 to +1.88. The lift is a level shift, which is exactly what headline 1 asserts.

R-D. The "cannot corroborate / changed segment AND direction" argument is wrong for the numbers actually published. The 3.1 table comes from sweep_s2.json, which PREDATES sign locking (sign_locked absent in s2, true in s3), and the recorded sign for seg_hiliq_p is -1 for all 15 factors in s2. With sign -1 the long book takes the BOTTOM of the lexicographic panel, so the +1 shift cs_first_high40 gives the top-40%-amount names pushes them OUT of the book. Verified twice: (i) synthetic panels through partura.ops_ext — the s2 seg_hiliq_p book holds 0% of its names in the top-40% amount, 100% in the bottom 60%, mean factor-rank of held names 0.082 versus seg_lowliq_m's 0.135 (same direction), and 61% of its names are the same names seg_lowliq_m holds; (ii) the repo's own anatomy, /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/runs/F101_day_shine_retstd/anatomy_s2.json, where the published seg_hiliq_p book's held_share by amount quintile is 39.5% / 37.5% / 20.9% / 2.0% / 0.003%. So the report's label "push the top four tenths of amount to the back" is accurate for the run it published, the two rows are the same economic action, and they do corroborate each other. (Also: "s2 and s3 completely identical" is true for seg_lowliq_m / seg_lowliq_p / v_base / k_known but false for seg_hiliq_p and seg_hiliq_m, where all 15 factors differ — the reporter did not check.)

R-E. The factor-free allocation term the reporter asks to add already exists in the repo: anatomy_*.json segments[*].ew_excess gives the equal-weight excess per 20-day-amount quintile with no factor at all — bottom 20% +15.09%/yr, 20-40% +8.92%, 40-60% +2.61%, 60-80% -6.02%, top 20% -17.80% — and signals[*].seg[*].tilt/held_share gives each book's overweight (k_known itself holds 99.9% of its book in the bottom amount quintile). This is a direct, factor-free confirmation of headline 1's claim that the current reward pays for the liquidity tilt.

WHAT SURVIVES, and why it changes nothing: the conditional median on base>=1 really is +0.41 rather than +1.18, so the lift is smaller on bases that already work. But /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/research/alpha_distillation/B01_reverse_guidance.md:7 declares the paired convention up front, the sentence "lifts it whatever factor it is wrapped around" is literally true once the direction is matched (15/15 positive, 0% down, 100% both segments up), R2's cited counts in guidance/B01.yaml:30 (13/15 up, 14/15 both) are correct, and a shrinking d as the base improves is arithmetically forced by a near-constant variant level — which is the report's own point, not a counter-argument. Also note the reporter's "did not beat the known pool" observation does not contradict headline 1: headline 1 is about what the reward pays for, and 12/15 landing under the Amt family is consistent with "this is the same money as the Amt family".

Scripts and outputs (nothing outside tmp/review was written, no commits, no server): /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/verify/refute-seg-regression/v1.py (+out_v1.txt) paired stats, base>=1 subset, direction-matched recomputation, k_known comparison, s2-vs-s3 diff; v2.py (+out_v2.txt) per-id sign/sign_locked/expr diff that exposes the s2 unlocked sign; v3.py (+out_v3.txt) synthetic _lexi/sign semantics and book overlap; v4.py (+out_v4.txt) segment ew_excess and per-signal book tilts; v5.py (+out_v5.txt) independence and regression-to-mean null models.

result.corrected_fix:
The filed defect needs no fix to headline 1 or to guidance/B01.yaml R2: both the number (+1.18) and the conclusion survive direction-matching, and the reporter's own "variant sharpe is nearly base-independent" observation is the strongest form of the claim it attacks. Do not condition the headline on base>=1 (n=5, and the subset's mean was driven by a mislabeled case), and do not swap the seg_hiliq_p companion row for seg_hiliq_m — for the run that was published, seg_hiliq_p already IS the direction-matched low-amount action.

Two smaller, genuinely number-changing issues surfaced while refuting, both in the stats layer rather than in the conclusion:

1. /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/motif_stats.py pairs a fixed variant id per factor, but the seg_*/scr_* "_m"/"_p" suffix is the sign applied inside the locked-sign expression (scripts/sweep.py:111-116 plus the lock at sweep.py:146-150), not the factor's own direction. Any factor whose v_base sign is +1 (F111 here, 1 of 15) therefore enters every seg_*/scr_* row with the reversed direction. Fix: pick the direction-matched id per factor (seg_X_m when v_base sign < 0, seg_X_p otherwise), or aggregate the better of the two and say so. Effect on the published 3.1 table: seg_lowliq_m becomes mean +1.28, down 0%, both 100% (median unchanged at +1.18); seg_hiliq_m goes from med -1.04 to med -1.60.

2. The 3.1 table mixes two vintages. seg_lowliq_* is bit-identical between sweep_s2 and sweep_s3, but seg_hiliq_*, seg_new_* and scr_* changed completely once sign locking landed (seg_hiliq_p +1.01 -> -3.18, seg_new_p +0.41 -> large negative), because in s2 the rank IC was still free to flip these lexicographic panels. Fix: state the tag on the table and regenerate the sign-locked rows from s3, or annotate each seg_*/scr_* row with the sign it was scored at. Headline 1 is unaffected either way — in s3 the low-amount segment stays positive and the high-amount segment is worse still (direction-matched seg_hiliq med -1.18).

The reporter's suggestion to add a factor-free segment-allocation item is already served by existing data: anatomy_*.json segments[*].ew_excess (bottom amount quintile +15.09%/yr, top -17.80%/yr) and signals[*].seg[*].tilt/held_share. Cite those in headline 1 instead of adding a cs_first_low40(constant, LIQ) variant.
